# QFRONT reference observations

Inspected 2026-10-07. References are links only; no reference photo is embedded
in the deliverable, its materials, source `.blend`, preview renders or GLB.

## Primary reference actually inspected

- Owner/property page: [TOKYU REIT — QFRONT](https://www.tokyu-reit.co.jp/portfolio/detail?id=1)
- Direct photograph: [TOKYU REIT property photograph, 1600 × 1227](https://www.tokyu-reit.co.jp/file/index?id=314&type=54)
- Inspection method: opened the actual full photo in the cloud browser and
  visually inspected its pixels; the building's front and left flank, ground
  entry and crown are clearly visible. This is not an image-search description.
- Image credit: TOKYU REIT property website; no photographer credit is visible
  at the linked property record. Site footer states “All rights reserved.”
- Reuse position: **reference-only, not licensed for redistribution here**.
  No photograph download or cropped/baked derivative is included in this repo.

Observed form and response in this original asset:

1. A broad, gently convex principal frontage above a tight street corner.
   The model uses a 28 m chord with a 3.2 m sag, both inferred, rather than an
   exact survey curve or footprint.
2. Fine bright continuous verticals with horizontal slab lines behind them.
   The model uses 2 m mullion spacing and lighter intermediate rails.
3. An integrated dark screen field occupying much of the upper middle facade.
   The model uses an original screen geometry field from 18.25 to 31.6 m,
   with cyan/coral abstract art and fictional words.
4. Large lower glazed retail openings with diagonally expressed framing,
   recessed doors, and an overhanging corner entry/canopy.
5. Transparent-looking glass crown above the media field and slim lateral
   floodlight arms. Roof equipment beyond the visible top is **not established
   by this photo**; the model's service enclosure and ventilation units are
   original plausible simplifications.

## Verified owner facts, not direct model dimensions

The property page identifies eight above-ground floors and three basement
levels, site area 784.26 m², total floor area 6,675.52 m² and October 1999
completion. These facts support the scale/category of the inspiration, but do
not establish the actual facade width, building height or roof plan. This asset
only suggests eight above-ground levels and does not claim dimensional fidelity.

## Supporting context

[GO TOKYO official guide](https://www.gotokyo.org/en/spot/366/index.html) identifies
the crossing-facing landmark, giant display and lower café uses. Used as
architectural-use context, not a source for brand reproduction or dimensions.

## Original content and dependencies

All geometry, procedural screen forms, generic fictional signage, materials and
preview compositions were created for this task. Blender's bundled Bfont is
converted to mesh for the short labels. No texture images, external font files,
real-world logos or brand artwork are bundled. Reference copyright does not
imply permission to redistribute those photos; obtain a suitable licence if a
future version introduces photographic textures.
